acceptance: A first-run and repeat-run fixture complete with zero decisions-table interaction; `inspect/explain` returns every decision and reason. A build that blocks on, auto-opens as mandatory, or cannot expose the table fails.
requirement: Routine audit/compile/start flows MUST NOT require the user to complete or acknowledge a detailed decisions table; the same detailed table MUST remain available through an explicit explain/inspect action.

acceptance: With known TaskSeal bytes plus an injected harness prefix unavailable to TaskSeal, terminal and JSON outputs report the exact controlled amount and label the remainder unknown/external; any “all boot tokens”, recovered-total, or inferred-removal claim fails.
requirement: Audit output MUST label TaskSeal-controlled context bytes/tokens separately from harness/system/unobservable boot context and MUST NOT report the latter as recovered, removed, or fully measured.

acceptance: Release audit resolves each named threat to at least one current control/test or an explicit residual risk, verifies the reporting route, and rejects any missing threat class, dead evidence link, private detail leak, or claim stronger than its test.
requirement: v0.1 public documentation MUST contain a concise threat model naming protected assets, trust boundaries, attacker-controlled inputs, HOME/parent contamination, path/symlink escape, malicious context, adapter/provider drift, secret/private-data leakage, digest/receipt forgery, mitigations, residual risks and security-reporting route.

acceptance: A pinned snapshot compiles byte-identically with the distributor unavailable; a changed digest, unreviewed version, network fetch, or live-response-dependent compile refuses. A local overlay committed into portable policy also fails.
requirement: Any future central/team policy distribution MUST materialize a reviewed, versioned, digest-pinned vendored snapshot before compile; compile MUST NOT query or trust a live central authority. Portable project/scope/profile configuration remains committed, while local overlays remain private.

acceptance: Registry validation rejects omission or invalidity of each named field; registry/code divergence fails; a tuple passes only when its probes pass. A delivery observation promoted to support/capability without qualification fails the claims gate.
requirement: Every canonical adapter descriptor MUST record stable adapter ID, qualification status, output transport, supported harness/version ranges, capability probes, render-template ID/version, context precedence and isolation requirements. Delivery observations MAY be recorded only as optional observations and MUST NOT be emitted as guaranteed capability.

acceptance: A generated-contract fixture with no predeclared numeric criterion or no reproducible measurement fails; one meeting the frozen criterion and `GOV-09` disclosure passes; the same measurement below threshold fails.
requirement: Generated code for a small contract is forbidden unless P03 first freezes a numeric payoff criterion and records the generator, reproducible command, owned output and measured result meeting that criterion; absent a frozen criterion, handwritten/simple derivation wins.

acceptance: Dependency, CLI, registry and package scans find no runtime plugin loading, marketplace endpoint or install command; a planted dynamic loader/marketplace path fails. A statically registered adapter does not fail.
requirement: TaskSeal MUST NOT ship a dynamic plugin marketplace or dynamic plugin ABI. P17 may define a typed static contribution contract only after its real external-adapter trigger; any marketplace/ABI requires a separate later authority decision.

acceptance: Repeated inference from identical configuration is byte-identical; a valid override deterministically wins and appears in provenance; an undeclared, environment-derived or unrecorded override fails.
requirement: Artifact-affecting metadata MUST be derived deterministically from governed configuration; an explicit governed override MAY replace an inferred value and MUST be recorded with source and reason.

acceptance: Deleting the cache leaves compiled bytes unchanged; poisoning an entry cannot alter an approved decision and is detected/recomputed; a cache-only value entering authority or output fails.
requirement: Caches MAY contain measurements and derived results but MUST NOT be an authority source or change approved effective configuration/compiled bytes.

acceptance: Schema rejects each omitted field, invalid date, rate without numerator/denominator, unknown status or stale contract digest; selector rejects experimental/revoked entries and accepts a fully matching qualified tuple.
requirement: A v0.2 analyzer qualification registry MUST bind runner, provider, model/version, test date, analyzer contract digest, supported envelope, protected/evidence/schema pass numerators and denominators, price-card date, and status `qualified`, `experimental`, or `revoked`; only qualified non-revoked entries may be selected.

acceptance: Before an owner resolution, any relevance-based exclusion path fails. After resolution, metaschema/owned-URI checks pass, unknown properties and each missing required field fail, every valid enum value round-trips, and bad ID/digest/enum vectors fail.
requirement: No runtime filtering is authorized. If the `A11-04` owner conflict is resolved in favor of applicability records, P11 MUST freeze an owned/versioned Draft-2020-12 closed record requiring `schema_version`, `item_id`, `item_kind`, `content_digest`, `class`, `filter_policy`, `conditions`, `analysis`, `approval`, and `provenance`; IDs use the stated 3–200 grammar, digests are lowercase `sha256:` plus 64 hex, item kind and class use the source closed enums, and filter policy is `always/conditional/never/quarantined`. The `taskseal.example` URI is forbidden.

acceptance: Duplicate/empty/81-char tags, invalid pins, duplicate/invalid superseded IDs and overlong notes fail; a protected/required/unknown `exclude` fixture fails while a permitted reviewed pin round-trips.
requirement: Descriptive tags are unique nonempty strings ≤80 and default empty; `owner_pin` is `none/include/exclude/quarantine` and defaults `none`; superseded IDs are unique valid IDs and notes are ≤4,000. `exclude` on protected, required or unknown material MUST be rejected, never silently prioritized.

acceptance: One vector per discriminator passes; duplicate/empty/overlong strings and invalid risk fail; an all-empty conditional fixture fails exclusion authorization and is reported as conservatively included.
requirement: conditions` is closed and carries scope IDs, task domains, phases, languages, tools, capabilities and `minimum_risk`; string sets are unique 1–300 character values and risk is `low/medium/high/critical`. An approved `conditional` record MUST contain at least one nonempty schema-valid discriminator plus reviewed evidence; all-empty conditions are invalid and conservatively included.

acceptance: Omission, unknown property, confidence outside 0–1, invalid digest/date/line bound/status/source kind, duplicate evidence ref or empty reason fails; stale/unknown/unreviewed records cannot authorize exclusion.
requirement: analysis` is closed and records state `approved/stale/unknown`, nonempty analyzer contract, source digest, confidence 0–1, unique evidence refs and nonempty reason ≤4,000; `approval` is closed with status `unreviewed/approved/rejected/superseded` and bounded nullable receipt/approver/date-time fields; `provenance` is closed with source ID/kind/ref/digest, positive line bounds and source kind `project/user-snapshot/org-policy/generated/imported/native-skill`.

acceptance: P02 may expose only the frozen seam. Full-schema validation rejects unknown properties, omission of each listed field, bad ID/version bounds, empty layer list or invalid `created_at`; wording/claims tests reject causal-effectiveness or mutable-history claims.
requirement: The deferred receipt is an immutable privacy-first observation, never causal proof, using an owned/versioned Draft-2020-12 closed object with required `schema_version=1`, `receipt_id`, `taskseal_version`, `compiler_contract`, `adapter`, task-packet and manifest digests, `mode`, `profile_id`, decisions, coverage, run state, acceptance, privacy, nonempty layer digests, runner and date-time `created_at`; IDs/versions obey the source bounds.

acceptance: Each valid layer round-trips; missing adapter/layer field, bad enum/digest, empty adapter value, overlong harness/parent ID or extra property fails.
requirement: Receipt adapter data is closed and requires bounded nonempty ID/version with nullable bounded harness version; task/manifest/layer digests are lowercase SHA-256; each closed layer entry requires digest plus layer `L0/L1/L2/L3/skills-index/skills-detail` and optional nullable scope ID; parent receipt ID is nullable bounded.

acceptance: Omission of any list, extra property, duplicate/invalid entry, missing reason, bad digest or malformed coverage set fails; totals reconcile to the compiled decision ledger and protected/unknown omissions fail.
requirement: Receipt decisions are closed and require `included`, `excluded`, `unknown_kept`, `protected_included`; each entry is closed with bounded item ID/reason code and optional valid digest. Coverage is closed and requires scope IDs, path globs, domains and capabilities.

acceptance: Deterministic no-runner and observed-runner vectors round-trip distinctly; omitted/extra fields, nonboolean observation, inferred identity marked observed, or `unknown` interpreted as a real runner fails.
requirement: Runner is closed and requires `kind` and boolean `observed_not_inferred`. P02/P12 MUST define an explicit truthful deterministic/no-runner representation; `unknown` MUST NOT imply a runner, and no receipt may misstate execution identity.

acceptance: Valid vector per status passes; negative duration/count, end-before-start, inconsistent duration, wrong type, or started/completed/imported state missing its required times fails and cannot support completion.
requirement: Run state is closed and requires status, start/end, duration, nonnegative recompile count and scope-escape boolean. Status is `prepared/started/completed/interrupted/abandoned/imported`; canonical validation enforces status-dependent required timestamps, ordered times and duration consistency.

acceptance: Empty, duplicate-ID, bad-status/bounds/digest vectors fail; a receipt containing only skipped/not-run required checks cannot be completed; a complete declared set of executed results with matching evidence passes.
requirement: Acceptance is a nonempty array of closed results requiring acceptance ID and status `pass/fail/skipped/not-run/error`, with source-declared nullable bounded exit code, duration, evidence digest and summary. Completed acceptance requires every declared required result executed and no required `skipped/not-run`.

acceptance: Every action/kind valid vector passes; unknown action/kind, missing reason, bad digest, forbidden extra field or `none` carrying a contradictory produced-output claim fails.
requirement: Each manual override is closed and requires item ID, action `include/exclude/quarantine/reclassify` and nonempty reason; overrides default empty. Output reference is closed with kind `none/commit/patch/artifact` and source-declared nullable bounded reference/digest fields.

acceptance: Public vectors with any storage boolean true fail; private snapshot storage without consent or retention record fails; redaction references must resolve; a consented private vector remains outside public export and passes.
requirement: Privacy is closed and requires mode, booleans `raw_prompts_stored`, `source_snapshots_stored`, `absolute_home_paths_stored`, and redactions. Public receipts require all three storage booleans false. Source snapshots default false and may be stored only in an explicit consented private mode with a separate retention boundary; raw snapshots never enter a public receipt.

acceptance: Metaschema/owned-URI checks pass; unknown fields, each missing required field, wrong version, invalid ID/objective/output bounds or duplicate/empty/overlong guidance fails; valid single- and multi-scope packets pass.
requirement: L3 task packet v2 is an owned/versioned Draft-2020-12 closed object for one atomic task across one or more scopes/write sets and requires `schema_version=2`, 3–160-character valid task ID, nonempty objective ≤12,000, boundaries, budget and task characteristics; optional output format is ≤4,000 and tool guidance is a unique nonempty ≤2,000 string array defaulting empty. `taskseal.example` is forbidden.

acceptance: Valid empty/nonempty optional scope vectors pass; missing required arrays, duplicate/empty/overlong strings, duplicate scope IDs or an approval-required action executed without an exact receipt fails.
requirement: boundaries` is closed and requires unique nonempty bounded `must_not` and `owner_approval_required` strings; optional read-only scope IDs are unique and default empty.

acceptance: Boundary-minus-one/boundary vectors for every numeric field validate as specified; any other overflow action fails; byte/rule overflow returns refusal and leaves no artifact.
requirement: budget` is closed and requires `max_context_bytes≥1024`, `max_rules≥1`, optional estimated tokens ≥256, and `on_overflow=refuse`; overflow MUST occur before partial output.

acceptance: Every risk value and valid set round-trips; missing required set/risk, duplicate/empty/overlong string, unknown risk or extra field fails.
requirement: task_characteristics` is closed and requires domains, phases, capabilities and risk; domains/phases/capabilities/languages/tools are unique bounded string sets and risk is `low/medium/high/critical`.

acceptance: Valid cross-OS vectors normalize identically; omission, duplicate, absolute/HOME/`..` escape, backslash-divergent or unresolved scope vector fails before acceptance.
requirement: Coverage is closed and requires scope IDs, path globs, domains and capabilities. Paths/globs are slash-normalized root-relative values; absolute, HOME-relative, escaping or platform-divergent forms refuse.

acceptance: Valid absent/start-only/range vectors pass; empty/absolute/HOME/escaping path, zero/negative/reversed lines, overlong reason or extra field fails.
requirement: Line hints default empty; each closed hint requires a nonempty normalized root-relative path, optional positive start/end with start ≤ end, and optional reason ≤1,000.

acceptance: Empty is accepted only for the base type; empty nonempty-set, duplicate, zero-length or 1,001-character values fail; 1- and 1,000-character boundary values pass.
requirement: The reusable task-packet string-set type contains unique 1–1,000-character strings and defaults empty; its nonempty variant requires at least one item.

acceptance: PASS only if canonical fixtures round-trip through an independent DSSE v1.0.2 implementation; both required base64 alphabets verify; generic and valid registered predicate-specific payload types pass; missing/unsupported/mismatched/case-mutated `payloadType`, altered payload bytes, security reliance on `keyid`, missing/altered DSSE fields or a bespoke top-level envelope fail. Otherwise FAIL.
requirement: Every TaskSeal bundle attestation and assurance receipt crossing the governed seam MUST use the DSSE v1.0.2 JSON envelope and protocol. TaskSeal producers MUST emit `payloadType=application/vnd.in-toto+json`; consumers MUST accept that form and MAY accept `application/vnd.in-toto.<predicate>+json` only when `<predicate>` is the exact registered predicate filename. `payloadType` and exact decoded payload bytes are authenticated together; `keyid` is only an unauthenticated key-selection hint and MUST NOT drive a security decision. Standard and URL-safe base64 payload/signature encodings MUST both verify. Bespoke, look-alike and parallel envelopes are forbidden, and no private Praxis vocabulary enters the public schema.

acceptance: PASS only if an independent in-toto Statement v1.2 validator accepts the base payload, accepts a planted unknown Statement extension field, and TaskSeal profile validation also accepts the canonical payload; wrong/missing `_type`, missing `subject[]` or `predicateType`, or replacement of the Statement contract fails base validation, while missing `predicate` may pass base validation but MUST fail the TaskSeal profile and a forbidden field inside the separately closed TaskSeal-owned predicate fails only that profile. Otherwise FAIL.
requirement: The decoded DSSE payload MUST set `_type` exactly to `https://in-toto.io/Statement/v1` and satisfy the in-toto Attestation Framework v1.2.0 Statement v1 base contract, including required `subject[]` and `predicateType`. Base consumers MUST ignore unrecognized Statement extension fields and MUST NOT treat their presence as a base-shape failure. Although base Statement v1 permits an absent `predicate`, the stricter TaskSeal producer/profile MUST require `predicate` to preserve `NS01-001`. Any closed-shape restriction belongs only to a versioned TaskSeal-owned predicate profile, never to base Statement validation.

acceptance: PASS only if exact `payloadType` plus exact payload bytes verify, a one-byte mutation to either fails, semantically equal differently serialized JSON fails without a verification canonicalization/reserialization path, the verified byte sequence is the one consumed by the application, and any JCS-producing implementation passes the pinned errata vectors. Otherwise FAIL.
requirement: Signing and verification MUST use DSSE v1.0.2 `PAE(UTF8(payloadType), payload)` over the exact received payload bytes; the application MUST consume the same verified bytes. Verification MUST NOT parse/reserialize JSON or apply JCS/RFC-8785 before signature verification. If a producer separately uses RFC 8785/JCS before freezing payload bytes, P02/P07 vectors MUST pin the standard and verified errata 6292 and 7920, including negative-zero behavior; producer canonicalization never changes exact-byte verification.

acceptance: PASS only if instrumentation proves signer input equals transported payload for every vector and a double-serialization fixture with changed order/escaping refuses before emission; otherwise FAIL.
requirement: A producer MUST give the signer and transport the same immutable payload byte sequence; two independent serializations of one object are forbidden.

acceptance: PASS only if the HMAC-mode golden has empty `signatures[]`, a separately labelled verifiable MAC, and no DSSE signature entry, and a MAC-in-`signatures[]` fixture fails; otherwise FAIL.
requirement: While authentication is symmetric, the HMAC MUST sit beside the DSSE envelope, explicitly labelled as a shared-secret integrity tag, while DSSE `signatures[]` remains empty; the HMAC MUST NOT imitate a DSSE signature.

acceptance: PASS only if local integrity may be reported separately while the external fixture returns a stable refusal and never an authenticated/signed result; otherwise FAIL.
requirement: An external verifier MUST refuse an envelope with empty `signatures[]` and only the private symmetric tag; HMAC verification MUST NOT produce an external-authenticity or signed verdict.

acceptance: PASS only if pre-trigger private HMAC mode is allowed, external emission refuses without an independently verifiable Sigstore keyless signature, and a valid signature verifies independently; otherwise FAIL.
requirement: Before the first receipt is consumed outside the private trust domain, that receipt path MUST transition to Sigstore keyless OIDC signing. The trigger is the external-consumption event, not a date; no external receipt may remain HMAC-only or unsigned.

acceptance: PASS only if the registry proves ownership, uniqueness and version for every URI and rejects same-URI breaking mutation or ecosystem-URI impersonation; otherwise FAIL.
requirement: Every TaskSeal or receipt predicate MUST use a stable versioned URI in an owned namespace. A breaking shape change requires a new URI, and no ecosystem URI may label a different shape.

acceptance: PASS only if two implementations reproduce the vector, archive mtime/order/uid changes do not change it, and any included path or file digest mutation does; otherwise FAIL.
requirement: bundle_digest` MUST be SHA-256 of concatenated `<path>\0<sha256hex>\n` records for every included file after canonical sorting; archive/container bytes and metadata MUST NOT substitute.

acceptance: PASS only if adversarial non-ASCII/case vectors yield the published order in two implementations and at least two locales and locale collation is rejected; otherwise FAIL.
requirement: Bundle records MUST sort by raw UTF-8 bytes of normalized relative paths, never locale, case-fold, filesystem order or archive order.

acceptance: PASS only if multilingual vectors round-trip byte-identically and invalid/replacement/platform-codepage fixtures refuse before digest emission; otherwise FAIL.
requirement: Bundle-record paths MUST be valid UTF-8 bytes before sorting/hashing; invalid UTF-8 MUST refuse rather than be replaced or decoded by a platform code page.

acceptance: PASS only if lowercase 64-hex passes and uppercase, mixed-case, short, long, prefixed or non-hex values fail before digest computation; otherwise FAIL.
requirement: Every SHA-256 value inside a bundle record or published per-file inventory MUST be exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters.

acceptance: PASS only if exactly the manifest is excluded, all other eligible files are included, recomputation succeeds, and manifest-included or other-file-omitted fixtures fail; otherwise FAIL.
requirement: The manifest recording `bundle_digest` MUST be excluded from the bundle inventory/digest input, and no other eligible file may be implicitly excluded.

acceptance: PASS only if URI/digest resolve and recompute and wrong/missing/contradictory dependency or placement in `subject[]` fails; otherwise FAIL.
requirement: A receipt consuming a TaskSeal bundle MUST identify it in predicate `resolvedDependencies[]` by URI and `digest.sha256` equal to recomputed `bundle_digest`; it MUST NOT appear in `subject[]`.

acceptance: PASS only if fields are present/schema-valid and match the executing compiler artifact and missing, stale, unparseable or mismatched values fail verification; otherwise FAIL.
requirement: Every TaskSeal manifest MUST record the exact compiler identity and version that produced it in stable machine-readable fields.

acceptance: PASS only if independent recomputation equals the field and mutation of any included file, inventory path or recorded digest fails verification; otherwise FAIL.
requirement: Every TaskSeal manifest MUST record exactly one `bundle_digest` equal to recomputation under `DIG-01`–`DIG-05`.

acceptance: PASS only if an independent minimal verifier reproduces the digest from published bytes and missing, reordered, duplicated, extra or hidden exclusions/digests fail; otherwise FAIL.
requirement: Every bundle publication MUST include the complete ordered per-file path/digest inventory and manifest-exclusion rule needed to recompute `bundle_digest` without TaskSeal code.

acceptance: PASS only if two independent entity-gate fixtures verify the same receipt from published artifacts, tampering any bound field fails, and runner-only state or absolute-path dependence is rejected; otherwise FAIL.
requirement: An adapter qualification receipt MUST use a runner-neutral portable schema binding adapter identity/version/OS, tested-artifact and placed-byte digests, checks/outcomes, evidence digests and verifier version. Any entity gate MUST verify it from published artifacts without the originating runner, mutable state or absolute host path.

acceptance: PASS only if both output digests trace to one approved source digest, a source change deterministically updates affected outputs, and independently authored or stale output refuses; otherwise FAIL.
requirement: One human-approved rule source MUST compile in one governed transaction into context prose and an enforcement/permission artifact; neither output may have an independent normative source. TaskSeal emits adapter configuration but does not become the runtime permission broker.

acceptance: PASS only if all three variants round-trip and missing, duplicate, unknown or compile-guessed tiers refuse before emission; otherwise FAIL.
requirement: Every approved rule MUST carry exactly one tier from the closed enum `Enforced`, `Stated`, `Explanatory` before reaching either artifact; fourth, missing, multiple or compile-inferred tiers are forbidden.

acceptance: PASS only if a real capability fixture blocks the action and prose-only, declared-only, unsupported or non-blocking configurations fail the Enforced claim; otherwise FAIL.
requirement: An `Enforced` rule MUST compile to a qualified adapter's real permission, denial or scoped-tool mechanism that mechanically prevents the forbidden action; prose, declaration or relevance checks do not qualify.

acceptance: PASS only if every Enforced rule contributes zero prose bytes while appearing in enforcement/mapping and duplicate prose or missing enforcement fails; otherwise FAIL.
requirement: A rule accepted as `Enforced` MUST be absent from context prose and contribute exactly zero context bytes; its normative representation remains in the enforcement artifact and attested mapping.

acceptance: PASS only if adversarial task/relevance vectors retain every Stated rule byte-for-byte and any relevance-dependent omission/truncation fails; otherwise FAIL.
requirement: A `Stated` rule MUST remain in context prose as an obligation and MUST NOT be omitted, shortened, reordered out or cut for task relevance.

acceptance: PASS only if an over-budget fixture removes Explanatory items first in the declared order, preserves all Stated/Enforced material, and refuses if still over budget; any other cut fails.
requirement: Only positively classified `Explanatory` rationale/citations are first eligible for deterministic budget removal. No Stated obligation or Enforced mapping may be removed; remaining protected overflow refuses.

acceptance: PASS only if current code/schema/CLI/goldens expose no relevance exclusion, the counterexample corpus retains all safety rules, and any future path lacking both authority and evidence fails release; otherwise FAIL.
requirement: Until the owner decision required by `A11-04` records the conflict resolution, TaskSeal MUST ship no relevance-based include/exclude path. Reopening relevance requires that explicit authority record plus `ENF-12` evidence that three-tier promotion leaves material savings unavailable. The accepted ADR is not silently superseded.

acceptance: PASS only if absent, unknown, stale and low-confidence classifications emit Stated obligations and only approved Explanatory items enter the cut set; otherwise FAIL.
requirement: An unclassified rule MUST default to `Stated`; only explicit positive `Explanatory` classification can make it cuttable.

acceptance: PASS only if every unsupported capability emits Stated with no enforcement claim and silent downgrade, partial mechanism or false Enforced status fails; otherwise FAIL.
requirement: If the selected adapter cannot actually enforce a rule, the rule MUST remain `Stated`; no weakened mechanism or retained `Enforced` claim is permitted.

acceptance: PASS only if all five values are present and match registry/emitted artifacts and missing, generic, stale or contradictory disclosure fails; otherwise FAIL.
requirement: Every `ENF-09` fallback MUST disclose rule identity, requested tier, actual tier, adapter tuple and non-enforceable capability reason in the artifact.

acceptance: PASS only if independent verification recomputes every digest/mapping and swapping either output, source, compiler or tier map fails; otherwise FAIL.
requirement: One attestation MUST bind approved-source digest, compiler identity/version, context-prose digest, enforcement-artifact digest and rule-to-tier/output mapping.

acceptance: PASS only if a known corpus yields exact reproducible values reconciling to its classified inventory and filtering is not evaluated before this measurement; otherwise FAIL.
requirement: Before any additional filtering is considered, `audit` MUST report reproducible raw counts, denominators and proportions for rules promotable to `Enforced` and for `Explanatory` rules among the non-Enforced remainder.

acceptance: PASS only if compile-fail fixtures reject a bare string, qualified IDs round-trip, same-role/different-entity values remain distinct, and public-marker scans find no private role value; otherwise FAIL.
requirement: The public Rust seam MUST represent generic role identity as `RoleId { entity, role }`; no governed compile API may accept an unqualified bare role string. Concrete Praxis roles/values remain private and absent from public fixtures, vocabulary and docs.

acceptance: PASS only if compile-fail tests reject `UnverifiedLayer`, digest mismatch cannot construct `VerifiedLayer`, and a matching digest permits compile; otherwise FAIL.
requirement: Rust layer inputs MUST transition `UnverifiedLayer -> VerifiedLayer` only after digest verification, and compile APIs MUST accept only `VerifiedLayer`.

acceptance: PASS only if compile-fail/schema fixtures prevent untiered rules from reaching render/enforcement and all three tiers serialize deterministically; otherwise FAIL.
requirement: Every Rust `Rule` that can reach an artifact MUST contain a typed `Tier`; an untiered rule MUST be unconstructable or rejected before artifact code.

acceptance: PASS only if byte/rule overflow returns the typed refusal without writes, callers must exhaustively handle it, and panic/truncation/success substitutes fail; otherwise FAIL.
requirement: Budget refusal MUST be a typed Rust return outcome carrying exceeded dimension and limit; it MUST NOT be truncation, panic, generic success or string-only control flow.

acceptance: PASS only if type/static inspection covers every artifact-reaching map, a planted `HashMap` fails, and randomized insertion orders produce identical bytes; otherwise FAIL.
requirement: Every Rust map whose iteration can affect artifact, manifest, digest-input or attestation bytes MUST use `BTreeMap`; `HashMap` is forbidden on those paths.

acceptance: PASS only if API/dependency inspection finds typed library errors, zero public/library `anyhow` propagation and `anyhow` confined to `main`, and planted violations fail; otherwise FAIL.
requirement: The Rust library MUST expose typed `thiserror` errors; `anyhow` MAY appear only in binary `main` orchestration and MUST NOT cross the public library API.

acceptance: PASS only if an exhaustive variant/code table mechanically matches runtime, each code has one stable meaning, and missing, duplicate, catch-all or changed mappings fail compatibility; otherwise FAIL.
requirement: From the first Rust release, every process failure exposed to callers MUST map from one typed error variant to one documented stable exit code; opaque catch-all mapping and undocumented code reuse are forbidden.

acceptance: PASS only if API/dependency scans find none, compile runs without an executor, and planted async code/dependency fails; otherwise FAIL.
requirement: The compile library and CLI MUST remain synchronous and introduce no async signature, executor, reactor or async-runtime dependency.

acceptance: PASS only if each emitted code resolves in its owning registry, pairwise range/allocation collision is empty, provider-result fixtures remain distinct, occupied allocation is refused, and public scans reveal no private meaning; otherwise FAIL.
requirement: Public TaskSeal, private Praxis/PCS integration and provider-native results MUST occupy disjoint versioned numeric namespaces with one owner per allocation. The public registry MUST expose only TaskSeal meanings and opaque reserved downstream/provider ranges; private meanings remain in P09. Integration MUST preserve provider results distinctly.

acceptance: PASS only if tighter-global, tighter-task, equal and absent-task vectors produce exact expected limits, attempted relaxation resolves to global, and overflow refuses before output; otherwise FAIL.
requirement: For each byte and rule-count dimension, effective task limit MUST be `min(global, task)` when both exist and the global limit when task override is absent; a task override MUST never relax global policy.

acceptance: A valid fixture returns PASS without mutation; one invalid fixture per checked class returns its stable code and safe action; before/after filesystem and configuration digests remain identical.
requirement: v0.1 provides a read-only `doctor` command that validates installation, configuration/schema readability, artifact integrity and adapter qualification prerequisites, then reports stable error codes and the smallest safe next action without repairing or mutating state.

acceptance: Release audit resolves every required statement/link, executes the exact quickstart against the release artifact and rejects stale commands, missing caveats or maturity overclaim.
requirement: Every public source release contains a top-level README that states what TaskSeal is and is not, gives tested install/first-run commands for the exact artifact, links security/support/license documentation and labels the release maturity honestly.

acceptance: Triage fixtures for all five classes route correctly, expose no private security content and meet the frozen review window; an untriaged expired fixture fails.
requirement: Public issue operations classify new reports as defect, feature, support, security or out-of-scope; security reports leave the public tracker, and every non-security item receives a recorded disposition or next action within a release-plan-defined review window.

acceptance: Ownership validation resolves every protected path, rejects an unowned protected path and blocks a protected-path change lacking the required review.
requirement: Repository governance defines CODEOWNERS and an owner-review protected set for security-sensitive paths; a change touching that set cannot satisfy the release gate without an authorized owner review.

acceptance: CI rejects missing/invalid sign-off and a negative-rights fixture, accepts valid attestation and contains no mandatory CLA gate without an approved superseding decision.
requirement: Contributions through v1.0 use DCO sign-off and contributor-rights attestation; a CLA is not required unless a later explicit legal decision records why it is necessary.

acceptance: Contribution schema rejects absent provenance and release review resolves every declared origin to its evidence and license/privacy disposition.
requirement: Every contribution declares the origin/provenance of nontrivial code or assets sufficiently to perform license, privacy and generated-content review.

acceptance: A generated/bulk fixture without any required field fails; a complete fixture reproduces or explains the delta inside the declared boundary and passes independent review.
requirement: Generated code and generated or mechanical bulk refactors are explicitly disclosed with generator/tool identity, reproducible command or method, owned output boundary and review strategy.

acceptance: Clean fixture produces a signed/annotated baseline tag; dirty fixture refuses the clean tag, emits the complete manifest and preserves all before/after state digests.
requirement: A clean baseline is anchored by an annotated tag; a dirty or uncommitted baseline cannot be tagged as clean and instead receives a forensic manifest that records HEAD plus dirty, untracked and stash state without altering it.

acceptance: Offline/instrumented runs observe zero telemetry endpoints, analytics files or tracking identifiers; compile remains network-free and no opt-in state exists without a separate approved feature.
requirement: TaskSeal core, compiler, audit and launcher emit no telemetry and perform no analytics or tracking by default; any future opt-in service remains separate, explicit and outside deterministic compile.

acceptance: Boundary-minus-one, boundary and boundary-plus-one fixtures on every advertised OS prove success/refusal, no partial output and no normalized-path collision.
requirement: Every advertised OS supports declared path-length boundaries; over-limit paths fail before partial publication with a stable error, and supported long paths produce byte-identical logical artifacts without truncation or collision.

acceptance: Repository scan finds no unapproved binary demo; release asset resolves to a script/source revision and digest, and deletion/retention follows the frozen policy.
requirement: Generated binary demo artifacts are not committed to ordinary Git history unless an explicit size/retention policy approves them; reproducible source scripts, text evidence and digests remain canonical, while published binaries use release assets or another owner-approved store.

acceptance: Accessibility gate resolves the transcript/captions, matches every scripted scene and command, and rejects a demo with omitted caveat or inaccessible-only information.
requirement: Every public audiovisual demo has a complete accessible text transcript or caption artifact that includes commands, relevant output, caveats and links to the exact release evidence.

acceptance: Fresh release review verifies the statement against the current owner-approved program status and rejects absent, stale or misleading bounty language.
requirement: SECURITY.md` truthfully states the current bounty status; while no funded program exists it explicitly says no bounty is offered and never implies payment.

acceptance: Create two profiles with conflicting pins, select each in turn, and prove distinct deterministic manifests; duplicate names are refused.
requirement: A single project may persist at least two uniquely named profiles; selecting a profile applies exactly that profile's base mode, include pins, exclude pins, and scope overrides without mutating another profile.

acceptance: A fixture with known component byte counts produces the exact total and components in terminal and JSON output; a validator proves `sum(components) = total`.
requirement: Read-only audit output reports total inherited-context size and a per-source/per-component size breakdown whose values sum exactly to the total.

acceptance: A representative change can traverse the documented workflow without a committee, heavyweight RFC, or generated ceremonial artifact, and a governance scan finds no such mandatory gate.
requirement: TaskSeal development governance uses direct accountable decisions, task-level plans, and consolidated review/gates; committees, mandatory heavyweight RFC ceremony, and ceremonial code generation are not required change gates.

acceptance: Release CI passes on the declared MSRV and stable lane; a fixture using a newer-than-MSRV feature fails the MSRV lane; an unrecorded MSRV bump fails the release gate.
requirement: Every source release declares one minimum supported Rust version (MSRV); required CI compiles/tests on that exact version and current stable Rust, and an MSRV increase requires an explicit compatibility decision and changelog entry.

acceptance: Architecture review inventories every custom trait/macro/nontrivial generic abstraction and fails if any lacks the required need, simpler alternative, and module explanation.
requirement: Nontrivial Rust modules must have plain-language module documentation; custom traits, macros, or generic abstraction beyond standard derives must link a demonstrated need and the simpler rejected alternative so the owner can follow the compile path without hidden cleverness.

acceptance: Repository/link scan finds no live unresolved `methodos` path or identifier outside an explicit migration alias/history allowlist; history-follow and link checks pass.
requirement: Rename the live method system from `methodos` to `exp-lab` while preserving Git history, historical names in evidence, and valid redirects or updated links for every live reference.

acceptance: Tier-policy fixtures select the lowest qualified tier and refuse an expensive-tier selection lacking lower-tier failure evidence or a matching risk rule.
requirement: exp-lab selects the cheapest qualified model tier that meets the task's recorded quality and evidence floor; a more expensive tier requires either a failed lower-tier qualification on the same task class or a recorded risk-class rule.

acceptance: One new and one existing non-TaskSeal fixture complete discovery→intake→init/lint→census; a hard-coded TaskSeal-only fixture fails the generality scan.
requirement: exp-lab entity discovery, intake, initialization, lint, and census accept registered arbitrary new or existing entities and contain no TaskSeal-specific discovery path.

acceptance: Valid role fixture is admitted; fixtures missing each required field are rejected.
requirement: A new exp-lab role may be registered only with a named entity-growth outcome, required inputs, produced artifact, and proving check; role labels without all four fields are refused.

acceptance: Search finds laws from two entities through links; a central copied law body fails the repository-boundary gate.
requirement: Cross-entity law discovery uses a generated/searchable metadata index containing entity, law ID, title, incident date, and entity-local link; it never copies another entity's KB or other organs into the center.

acceptance: In a cold resume drill, the operator identifies the correct next action from generated output within 120 seconds; the fixture contains no second manually maintained status store.
requirement: exp-lab derives a one-command resume checkpoint from authoritative journal, census, and experiment artifacts, showing current level, last checkpoint, blockers, and next `READY`/`OWNER` action without duplicate manual entry.

acceptance: Init/maturity advancement refuses an entity with no completed intake record and proceeds for a schema-valid intake fixture.
requirement: Every new or newly admitted existing entity completes an intake stage with lightweight research before maturity growth or live-mechanism work begins.

acceptance: Schemas accept every valid enum and reject cross-assigned values, including `maturity_level=L4+`.
requirement: Intake options use typed `intake_level = L0/L1/L2/L3/L4+`, distinct from typed `maturity_level = L0/L1/L2/L3`; neither field may be parsed or compared as the other.

acceptance: A complete record validates and round-trips; one invalid fixture per missing field and one unselected ladder are rejected.
requirement: A lightweight-research record contains the entity problem/outcome, current artifacts, relevant precedents, principal risks, and the L0–L4+ option ladder; it persists the owner's selected intake level with timestamp and provenance.

acceptance: Fleet inventory contains 3–5 entries; every entry resets to its pin and passes the offline preflight.
requirement: exp-lab maintains a ready fleet of three to five popular open-source project fixtures, each pinned to an exact revision and able to reset and pass preflight without network-dependent mutable state.

acceptance: A fleet-run validator rejects any run missing context inventory, a supported mode arm, quality value, or raw evidence link.
requirement: Every fleet run inventories project context files, exercises each TaskSeal mode supported by that fixture, and records a defined result-quality measure plus raw evidence for every arm.

acceptance: A maturity-raise run without an owner decision receipt refuses; a receipt naming entity and target level proceeds.
requirement: Only the owner selects which census candidate is next targeted for L2 or L3; automation may rank candidates but cannot activate the selection.

acceptance: Diff gate passes a single-entity single-transition fixture and rejects multi-entity, multi-level, or unrelated-file changes.
requirement: Each maturity raise is one isolated change for one entity and one target-level transition, grown through the governed entity-init workflow; unrelated entity files and additional level transitions are forbidden.

acceptance: Bare fixture scores exactly L0; adding only top-level `README.md` scores exactly L1; removing it returns L0.
requirement: Structural maturity starts at L0 for every entity and becomes L1 if and only if top-level `README.md` exists; higher levels require their separate substantive controls.

acceptance: Inventory classifies all nine classes and the boundary test rejects an instance stored outside its owning entity while accepting entity-local instances.
requirement: The nine governed method classes are bidirectional goldens, numbered KB laws, pending-promotions filing, RunRecordV1/runs ledger, passports, specimen-mining protocol, timed owner protocol, federated journal, and `EXPERIMENTS.md`; every instantiated class is stored with its owning entity, never as another entity's central organ.

acceptance: Valid README fixture passes; missing, placeholder-only, no-description, and no-first-law-link fixtures fail.
requirement: An entity's top-level `README.md` is created on day one, explains in substantive prose what the entity is, and links its first numbered law; comment-only/template-placeholder content does not satisfy L1.

acceptance: Law validation accepts a resolvable dated incident link and rejects invented, undated, or unlocatable incident fields.
requirement: A KB law may be created only from a real dated incident and must identify the incident location; no incident means no law.

acceptance: Parser accepts a complete Wall→Claim→Evidence→Law fixture and rejects missing/multiple claims, absent evidence paths, absent future rule, or absent golden link.
requirement: Every L2 KB law is numbered and contains exactly one falsifiable Claim, measured or observed Evidence with paths, and a future Law naming the golden that pins it, in addition to its Wall/incident.

acceptance: A method-path diff without exactly one new valid linked law fails; a non-method diff is exempt.
requirement: Every change to exp-lab method doctrine or method behavior is linked in the same change to one new numbered local KB law satisfying the incident-grounded law schema.

acceptance: Valid entity journal passes; generic placeholder, wrong-entity, missing-standard, and no-entry fixtures fail.
requirement: Substantive L3 requires an entity-scoped `journal/JOURNAL.md` that declares the federated journal standard and links at least one entity-specific checkpoint entry.

acceptance: Journal lint accepts an ordered valid fixture and rejects bad path shape, empty summary, duplicate line, or ascending date order.
requirement: journal/JOURNAL.md` links one entry per line in newest-first order; each link targets `entries/YYYY-MM-DD-slug.md` and includes a nonempty hook summary.

acceptance: Entity-specific check fixture passes; empty, comment-only, generic placeholder, and unresolvable-check fixtures fail.
requirement: Substantive L3 requires entity-specific `EXPERIMENTS.md` with at least one executable or mechanically verifiable prescribed check; a generic scaffold or placeholder cannot confer L3.

acceptance: Schema accepts all three values and rejects every other status or missing status.
requirement: Experiment-program entries use exactly `[DONE]`, `[READY]`, or `[OWNER]` as status values.

acceptance: Shipped-mechanism validator resolves both links and rejects fixtures missing either link or pointing to nonexistent artifacts.
requirement: Every mechanism declared shipped by an entity links one proving check and one measuring experiment.

acceptance: Resume receipt names the persisted item ID; an unlisted ad hoc item is refused unless accompanied by an approved program-change receipt.
requirement: On resume, an entity executes the next applicable item in its persisted experiment program; replacing the written program requires a reviewed change rather than an ad hoc run.

acceptance: Lint changes level for valid journal/experiments, never for optional bench directories, and rejects bench organs on an entity declared non-episode-running.
requirement: journal/JOURNAL.md` and substantive `EXPERIMENTS.md` are scoring L3 organs; `passports/`, `runs/`, and `schemas/` are optional, non-scoring bench organs permitted only for entities that run episodes.

acceptance: Allowlist scan accepts every listed center artifact and rejects one fixture for each forbidden foreign-organ class.
requirement: The exp-lab center allowlist is doctrine (`README.md` and center-local `kb/`), `scaffold/`, governed init/lint/census scripts, and generated `MATURITY.md`; another entity's KB, goldens, journal, experiments, passports, runs, or schemas are forbidden.

acceptance: Handoff gate passes a substantive L3 fixture and refuses fixtures with structural-only journal or experiment placeholders.
requirement: First owner handoff is forbidden until substantive L3 is proven: valid L2 proof, entity-specific journal/checkpoint, and entity-specific experiment program must all pass; structural placeholders do not count.

acceptance: Fault injection for command, unset-variable, pipeline, managed proof failure, and tolerated `chmod` produces the specified nonzero/refusal or explicit reported result for each tool.
requirement: exp-lab shell tools have explicit failure semantics: census and init fail on command, unset-variable, and pipeline errors; lint fails on unset-variable and pipeline errors and explicitly captures each ordinary command failure it is designed to score; every tolerated failure such as optional `chmod` is named and reported.

acceptance: Golden schema snapshot matches every required preamble field/column and rejects local-time, missing notice, missing column, or reordered incompatible schema.
requirement: Generated `MATURITY.md` has a frozen title, no-hand-edit notice, structural-only notice, UTC timestamp, and columns `Entity`, `Level`, `kb`, `goldens`, `journal`, and `EXPERIMENTS`.

acceptance: Argument/path matrix proves required argument, basename default, explicit name, missing-directory creation, arbitrary registered path, and unregistered-path refusal.
requirement: Governed entity-init requires one entity-directory argument, accepts an optional display name defaulting to the directory basename, creates a missing entity directory, and operates on any registered entity path rather than a product-specific path.

acceptance: Missing fixture reports `grown` with exact template rendering; existing-content fixture reports `keep` with byte-identical content.
requirement: Entity-init grows top-level `README.md` from the governed README template only when `README.md` is absent.

acceptance: Missing fixture creates both paths; existing journal/entry bytes remain unchanged and report `keep`.
requirement: Entity-init grows `journal/JOURNAL.md` only when absent and always ensures `journal/entries/` exists without altering existing entries.

acceptance: Missing fixture reports `grown` with exact template rendering; existing-content fixture reports `keep` with byte-identical content.
requirement: Entity-init grows top-level `EXPERIMENTS.md` from the governed experiments template only when absent.

acceptance: Run init twice over the full fixture; second run has zero `grown` records, all expected `keep` records, identical digest tree, and no duplicate paths.
requirement: Re-running entity-init is idempotent: every existing organ is reported as `keep`, no existing organ bytes change, and no duplicate organ is created.

acceptance: A fixture whose threshold is `failures == 0`, whose declared independent variable has two named arms, whose control is pinned, and whose fixture/capsule bytes match their recorded SHA-256 values validates before execution. Validation refuses each of: absent/duplicate experiment ID; empty or non-falsifiable hypothesis; threshold that cannot consume the declared result; observed variable or arm absent from the declaration; absent control; fixture or capsule digest mismatch; mutation of any frozen field after the first run receipt; and use of an intake-level value as a maturity or experiment field.
requirement: Before the first run effect, every private exp-lab experiment MUST persist one closed, versioned machine record containing a stable experiment ID, a falsifiable hypothesis, a machine-evaluable decision threshold, declared variables and controls, the exact fixture digest, and—when a capsule is used—the exact capsule digest. Once a run starts, that definition is immutable; a changed hypothesis, threshold, variable/control set, or digest creates a new version linked to its predecessor.

acceptance: Two executions of one pinned fixture produce receipts that resolve the same experiment/fixture identity while retaining distinct run IDs and measured values. Receipt verification recomputes every referenced digest and rejects: wrong branch/HEAD/artifact/model reachability under `LAB-16`; wrong runner or environment; interpretation bytes in the raw-result store; raw-result mutation after interpretation; absent verdict, cost, elapsed time, promotion/rejection event, or lineage; absent token count when the runner reports token consumption; a token count asserted for a runner that reports no token channel without an explicit truthful representation; and replacement of an earlier receipt rather than append-only correction. `A07-08` remains a plan parameter for any later public receipt and is not silently resolved here.
requirement: Every private exp-lab run MUST bind the `XPL-37` experiment version and the exact evidence identity required by `LAB-16`; record runner and environment identity; store raw result bytes separately from interpretation; record stand verdict, cost, elapsed time, token use when tokens were consumed, and exactly one promotion or rejection event; link parent/child lineage; and emit an append-only receipt whose digest binds all referenced artifacts.

acceptance: With network and all optional services disabled, a registered entity completes discovery, intake validation, one deterministic experiment, receipt verification, census, and resume from repository-local artifacts. Dependency and configuration inspection finds no required dashboard, central database, central orchestrator, or ML platform. A fixture that marks an unapproved taxonomy version as universally mandatory is refused; a local optional visualization that is removable without changing evidence or verdict remains allowed.
requirement: Core exp-lab discovery, intake, execution, evidence, census, and resume MUST remain operable from repository-local files and commands without requiring a heavy dashboard, central artifact database, universal orchestration runtime, or ML platform. A universal taxonomy MUST NOT be frozen before an explicit owner decision supported by demonstrated cross-entity need.

acceptance: The L2 gate executes one success golden and one designed refusal/failure golden, observes the expected opposite outcomes, reports collected count greater than zero for each, resolves both through the fixture manifest, resolves the incident→law→golden chain, and validates the associated experiment, run, and error records. It refuses when either golden is missing, skipped, zero-collected, non-hermetic, unexpectedly green/red, absent from the manifest, backed only by placeholder text, or when any referenced record or digest is invalid. `intake_level=L2` cannot satisfy this maturity gate, preserving `A07-14`.
requirement: Private `maturity_level=L2` MAY be awarded only when one real incident-derived law passes `XPL-17` and `XPL-18`; one hermetic success golden and one hermetic intentional-refusal/failure golden execute through the consolidated runner with positive collected cardinality and no required skip; the experiment/run records pass `XPL-37` and `XPL-38`; the private error ledger passes `XPL-48`–`XPL-50`; and a digest-bound fixture manifest resolves every executed fixture. Placeholders or structural presence alone never confer L2.

acceptance: A fresh L3 run executes the full enumerated lane with zero missing/skipped checks, demonstrates each planted negative is detected for its intended reason, validates stand self-checks, and cold-resumes to the same checkpoint and next action from the bound artifacts. The gate refuses and records quarantine for a skipped check, zero checks collected, a negative control that remains green, a self-check that observes only screen text, stale/wrong execution identity, non-deterministic resume, broken lineage, or structural journal/experiment placeholders.
requirement: Private `maturity_level=L3` MAY be awarded only after L2 passes and one consolidated no-skip lane executes stand self-checks and intentional negative controls. Any failed self-check or negative control quarantines the claim under `LAB-12`; the evidence MUST bind exact execution identity under `LAB-16`, resume deterministically under `XPL-06`, and preserve experiment→result→decision lineage under `XPL-38`.

acceptance: In a fixture where every L2 organ except the refusal golden is valid, census reports the individual organ states, `highest_passed=L1`, `blocked_target=L2`, the missing refusal golden as blocker, and the exact last L1 proof. Setting an aggregate score to 99% does not change that result. Census also refuses/marks blocked when proof cardinality is zero, the last-proof coordinate is unresolved or stale, a hard-gate field is omitted, or an atomic-write recovery fixture would truncate the prior valid census.
requirement: Generated private census output MUST report, separately, each required organ's completeness/proof state, the highest passed maturity gate, the blocked target gate, its exact blockers, and the last valid proof coordinate. A percentage or average score MAY be displayed only as non-authoritative detail and MUST NOT compensate for a failed hard gate or raise maturity.

acceptance: A deterministic hash question routes to D0 and rejects any model spend; a narrow classification with qualified D1 evidence stops at D1; a D1 result below its frozen quality floor records the failed criterion before D2; a stochastic claim requiring independence records repeated D3 runs; and D4 cannot activate without an exact owner/expert decision receipt. Fixtures that skip an applicable lower tier, cite expense as quality, use an unqualified model, or escalate without residual uncertainty/risk evidence fail before the higher-cost action.
requirement: Private experiment routing MUST attempt evidence tiers in order: `D0` deterministic check; `D1` cheapest narrow qualified model; `D2` strongest qualified model; `D3` repeated independent verification; `D4` owner/expert decision. Escalation is allowed only when the preceding applicable tier leaves recorded residual uncertainty or a predeclared risk rule requires the higher tier. Price alone is never evidence quality.

acceptance: Build a capsule from the frozen package fixture, verify every manifest member digest, resolve each exported law to its incident and guarding golden, execute all qualification goldens, and resolve the declared compatibility and license evidence. Verification rejects a missing required organ, unknown unmanifested member, changed member byte, duplicate identity/version, unresolved incident/golden, non-minimal reference that imports undeclared private state, incompatible license conclusion, or migration note that cannot identify the prior version and rollback path.
requirement: Every private capability capsule MUST be one versioned, digest-bound package containing identity, compatibility scope, accountable owner, license metadata, contracts, a minimal reference implementation, qualification goldens, exported laws with resolvable incident links, migration notes, and a SHA-256 member manifest. This is one supply-chain object contract, not ten permanent field controls.

acceptance: Search returns the existing capsule from the generated metadata index; inspect resolves its exact digest and compatibility evidence; adopt-plan executes every capsule golden against the adopter fixture and writes one receipt with all listed fields. Adoption refuses a copied law body, unresolved or mismatched digest, live-center dependency, unapproved newer version, compatibility inferred only from similar names, omitted local adaptation/deviation, or a golden that passes in the producer but fails or is skipped in the adopter.
requirement: Private capability search/inspect/adopt planning MUST expose existing indexed mechanisms before new implementation; MUST NOT copy law Markdown across entities, require a live central runtime, auto-update a capsule, or infer compatibility from naming similarity; MUST execute the capsule goldens in the adopter context; and MUST append an adoption receipt containing capsule ID, version, digest, adoption mode, local adaptations, compatibility result, and deviations.

acceptance: The five-option intake fixture yields one receipt with one selected option, the other four explicitly rejected, all listed decision fields populated, and an exact owner authorization bound to the same entity and option set. Activation refuses no selection, multiple selections, an omitted rejected option, absent/zero budget or timebox, missing kill/upgrade trigger, unresolved first experiment or checkpoint, stale/wrong-entity authorization, or substitution of `maturity_level` for `intake_level`.
requirement: Before private intake activation, the owner decision receipt MUST identify the selected level and every rejected level from the typed option set; required gates; exact budget and timebox; kill and upgrade triggers; first experiment ID; next checkpoint; decision timestamp; and provenance. It supplements, and does not weaken, `LAB-19` and `XPL-09`.

acceptance: The release candidate package passes a scanner fixture containing planted secret and personal-data values only after both are removed/redacted, inventories every captured surface, resolves all required notices to the rendered package, and records a dated legal review when the monetized brand-heavy trigger is true. Publication refuses an unresolved scanner finding, unrecorded non-neutral capture, missing modified-source notice, stale license evidence, or triggered brand-heavy monetization without the review receipt. A non-monetized neutral terminal/code/diff fixture does not require that receipt.
requirement: Before any exp-lab demo leaves the private boundary, the demo package MUST contain zero unresolved personal data or secrets; default visual capture MUST be limited to neutral terminal/code/diff surfaces unless an exception is recorded; all modified-source attribution/notice obligations MUST be satisfied; and a monetized campaign whose central creative relies on a third-party brand or logo MUST have a current designated legal-review receipt. This is private publication governance, not a public TaskSeal feature.

acceptance: Schema vectors accept ID lengths 3 and 200, sequence 1, entity length 1 and 200, summary lengths 1 and 2,000, absent/empty/12,000-character details, every exact enum value, and a valid RFC 3339 date-time; they reject ID lengths 2/201 or grammar violations, sequence 0/non-integer, entity length 0/201, summary length 0/2,001, details length 12,001, invalid date-time, wrong type/case, unknown enum, missing required field, and one unknown root property. Ledger vectors accept new event sequences `[1]` and `[1,2]`; they reject duplicate event ID, sequences `[1,3]`, `[2,1]`, or repeated `2`, any byte mutation/deletion of event 1, and an attempted in-place correction or redaction. Replay/closure refuses on every ledger-vector failure.
requirement: The private error-event schema MUST use JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 with a private non-public `$id`, a closed root object, and required fields `schema_version`, `event_id`, `error_id`, `sequence`, `event_type`, `entity_id`, `error_class`, `severity`, `summary`, `occurred_at`, `evidence_refs`, and `privacy`. Structural values retain the advisor v1 constraints: version is string `1`; event/error IDs are 3–200 characters matching `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:/-]*$`; sequence is integer ≥1; entity ID is 1–200 characters; summary is 1–2,000 characters; optional details are ≤12,000 characters; `occurred_at` is date-time; event type is exactly one of `ERROR_OBSERVED`, `ERROR_REPRODUCED`, `CAUSE_HYPOTHESIZED`, `STAND_INVALIDATED`, `FIX_PROPOSED`, `FIX_VERIFIED`, `LAW_PROMOTED`, `ERROR_SUPERSEDED`, `ERROR_RECURRED`, `ERROR_REOPENED`, `ERROR_CLOSED`; error class is exactly one of `STAND_LIED`, `UNDECLARED_FIXTURE`, `PORTABILITY`, `PACKAGING`, `SCOPE_ESCAPE`, `PRIVATE_TOPOLOGY_LEAK`, `MATURITY_OVERCLAIM`, `NOISY_CANONICAL_ARTIFACT`, `PRODUCT_DEFECT`, `PROCESS_DEFECT`, `SECURITY`, `PRIVACY`, `OTHER`; and severity is exactly `low`, `medium`, `high`, or `critical`. The authoritative ledger validator/storage layer—not JSON Schema—MUST enforce globally unique event IDs, immutable prior bytes, and monotonic contiguous sequence per error; corrections/redactions append events.

acceptance: A reproduced-error fixture resolves one evidence reference, exact runner/fixture identity and digests, affected run, reproducing experiment, promoted law, guarding golden, blast scope, and decision. Validation rejects zero evidence references, empty/overlong/duplicate collection entries, unknown nested properties, overlong environment fields, uppercase/short/long/non-hex digests, unknown blast scope/status, overlong descriptions/reason/action, and any unresolved referenced ID. An `ERROR_RECURRED` fixture must link both the earlier error and the distinct recurrence variant; an unlinked recurrence or closure with unresolved evidence fails replay/closure.
requirement: Every private error event MUST carry at least one unique non-empty evidence reference of at most 2,000 characters. Optional `observed_environment` is closed and may contain `os` ≤200, `arch` ≤100, `runner_id`/`fixture_id` ≤200, and runner/fixture digests matching `^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$`. Affected-run, experiment, related-error, law, and golden ID arrays contain unique 1–200-character IDs and default to empty. Optional closed `blast_radius` uses scope `single-run\|experiment\|entity\|fleet\|all-runs-with-stand\|unknown` and description ≤4,000. Optional closed `decision` uses status `open\|reproduced\|quarantined\|fixing\|verified\|closed\|superseded`, reason ≤4,000, and next action ≤4,000. Error-to-run, reproducing-experiment, promoted-law, guarding-golden, and recurrence-variant links MUST resolve before the corresponding claim or closure is accepted.

acceptance: Privacy vectors accept each exact classification with boolean `true` and `false`, absent/empty/2,000-character redaction notes, and no extra property; they reject missing classification/redacted, wrong case or unknown classification, non-boolean redacted, 2,001-character notes, and one unknown property. Export instrumentation proves zero raw-ledger reads or public writes without an exact approved projection receipt; fixtures containing a private identifier, role marker, absolute/private path, or topology token are removed or cause refusal. Merely setting `classification=public` never authorizes export.
requirement: Every private error event MUST contain a closed `privacy` object requiring `classification` and `redacted`; classification is exactly `public\|internal\|private\|secret`, redacted is boolean, and optional redaction notes are ≤2,000 characters. The event remains in the private ledger regardless of its classification label. No raw event, private identifier, role marker, path, or topology detail may enter public TaskSeal output. Any future sanitized projection requires a separate owner-approved projection schema, explicit allowlist/redaction transform, and verification receipt.

acceptance: PASS only if capture followed by read-back is byte-identical and its computed SHA-256 equals the recorded value; changing, normalizing, omitting, or appending one byte changes the digest and fails validation. Otherwise FAIL.
requirement: Private Milestone A authorization intake MUST preserve the received owner statement as an immutable raw-byte artifact and MUST record the SHA-256 of those exact bytes; no parser, renderer, or receipt generator may reconstruct or rewrite that artifact.

acceptance: PASS only if quoted and unquoted fixtures differing solely by the permitted marker match the same authorization, while doubled markers, inserted non-whitespace, deleted content, or any raw-artifact mutation fail. Otherwise FAIL.
requirement: For semantic authorization matching only, the private validator MAY remove a Markdown blockquote marker consisting of optional leading spaces, one `>`, and at most one following space from each quoted line; it MUST preserve every remaining byte and MUST retain the untouched raw artifact governed by `AUT-01`.

acceptance: PASS only if fixtures differing solely by permitted ASCII line-wrap whitespace match, while a changed digest digit, action byte, punctuation byte, token order, or non-ASCII character refuses before consumption. Otherwise FAIL.
requirement: For semantic authorization matching only, the private validator MAY collapse runs of ASCII space, tab, CR, and LF that represent prose line wrapping, including whitespace around the action and SHA-256 tokens; it MUST NOT alter token bytes, token order, punctuation, or the raw artifact.

acceptance: PASS only if paired renderings from one fixture contain identical approved facts/forms, the local-student output contains zero rationale fields or rationale prose, and the teacher/cloud output retains every required rationale. Otherwise FAIL.
requirement: A private exp-lab local-student rendering MUST contain only terse approved facts and executable forms and MUST omit explanatory rationale; the paired teacher/cloud rendering MUST retain the rationale for the same approved source items.

acceptance: PASS only if a transcript/commit fixture proves first action is a tool call, the plan file predates implementation changes, no intermediate conversational prose appears, and exactly one prose report follows the final verified commit; every violated ordering fails. Otherwise FAIL.
requirement: A qualified private local-worker turn MUST begin with a tool call, persist its plan in the assigned file before implementation, and emit conversational prose only once after its final verified commit.

acceptance: PASS only if broker expansion equals the two frozen command patterns and negative fixtures for bare Bash, wildcard Bash, and an extra command all refuse; conductor verification must observe the same expansion. Otherwise FAIL.
requirement: The private Praxis `task-report` capability MUST expand to exactly command-scoped `praxis-state.sh task-ack` and `praxis-state.sh task-decline` grants and MUST NOT grant bare Bash, wildcard Bash, or any third command.

acceptance: PASS only if the frozen role matrix grants `task-report` to every and only task-receiving roles, a missing receiver grant fails, and the verifier's effective grants are byte-identical before and after task-report resolution. Otherwise FAIL.
requirement: Every private Praxis role that can receive a task MUST have the `task-report` capability; a role already holding broader `bash-test` authority MUST receive no additional grant from `task-report`.

acceptance: PASS only if state history shows the matching acknowledgement transition precedes the first work effect; absent, late, or wrong-task acknowledgement fails. Otherwise FAIL.
requirement: A private Praxis task-receiving role MUST persist acknowledgement for the exact task before beginning task work.

acceptance: PASS only if every blocked fixture records a decline for the exact task with a nonempty reason and fixtures with silence, prose-only refusal, or acknowledgement-then-abandonment fail. Otherwise FAIL.
requirement: A private Praxis task-receiving role that cannot perform the task MUST issue `task-decline` with a nonempty reason instead of acknowledging or remaining silent.

acceptance: PASS only if state-backed ack/decline fixtures pass and identical panel prose without the state transition remains unacknowledged and fails. Otherwise FAIL.
requirement: Private Praxis acknowledgement and decline are valid only when the matching state-store transition succeeds; prose in panel output MUST NOT substitute for persisted state.

acceptance: PASS only if a supplied taskId produces one exact ACK-FIRST block with all matching identifiers before a byte-identical body, while missing/wrong/duplicate identifiers fail. Otherwise FAIL.
requirement: Private Praxis `send` MUST accept an optional `taskId`; when present it MUST prepend the canonical ACK-FIRST block containing the exact program, task, and panel identifiers before the unchanged task body.

acceptance: PASS only if the frozen four-argument corpus produces byte-identical injector calls, ledger entries, and result values before and after the API extension. Otherwise FAIL.
requirement: Adding optional `taskId` MUST preserve the behavior and argument interpretation of every existing four-argument private Praxis `send` call.

acceptance: PASS only if call-site/static analysis finds zero caller-built ACK-FIRST blocks and all taskId call paths traverse the single send composer; a caller-built fixture fails. Otherwise FAIL.
requirement: Only the private Praxis `send` primitive MAY compose ACK-FIRST transport text; callers MUST pass identifiers and task content and MUST NOT construct, prepend, or mutate the block themselves.

acceptance: PASS only if one live headless and one live iTerm fixture observe the exact expected value inside the receiver, with no literal placeholder, sender-side substitution, absence, or cross-panel value. Otherwise FAIL.
requirement: PX_PANEL_ID` MUST be set to the exact receiving panel ID in both private Praxis headless and iTerm worker environments and MUST expand inside the receiver process rather than in the sender.

acceptance: PASS only if a fixture with successful ledger/invocation but zero receiver evidence returns QUEUED and every claim/parser treats it as non-delivery; missing ledger or invocation cannot return QUEUED. Otherwise FAIL.
requirement: QUEUED:<orderId>` in private Praxis MUST assert only that the named order was durably ledgered and injector invocation occurred; it MUST NOT assert receipt, delivery, execution, or acknowledgement.

acceptance: PASS only if matching persisted acknowledgement yields DELIVERED and fixtures with no ack, wrong task, wrong program, wrong panel, transport success only, or screen change never yield DELIVERED. Otherwise FAIL.
requirement: DELIVERED:<panelId>` in private Praxis MUST be emitted only after the state store contains acknowledgement for the exact program, task, and panel tuple.

acceptance: PASS only if baseline goldens for both refusal paths match the post-change result bytes, exit status, ledger effect, and zero-injection behavior exactly. Otherwise FAIL.
requirement: The private Praxis acknowledgement transport change MUST preserve the frozen pre-change result and exit behavior for `NO-PANEL` and `REFUSED-SELF`.

acceptance: PASS only if unset/zero returns QUEUED within the frozen nonblocking bound, positive bounded values never exceed their bound, and separate polling changes no send-path default. Otherwise FAIL.
requirement: PX_SEND_ACK_WAIT` MUST default to `0`, causing private Praxis `send` to return without waiting for acknowledgement; only an explicit caller MAY request a positive bounded wait or poll the state store separately.

acceptance: PASS only if two identical acknowledgements produce one transition plus one duplicate result and an identical post-first state digest; concurrent repeats must satisfy the same invariant. Otherwise FAIL.
requirement: Private Praxis `task-ack` MUST be idempotent for one program/task/panel tuple: the first pending transition completes it, and every repeat MUST report duplicate without changing completed state or timestamps.

acceptance: PASS only if forced timeout reaches the injector exactly once, records the hint, and returns according to later transport evidence, while no timeout fixture takes an abort branch. Otherwise FAIL.
requirement: Expiry of the private Praxis injector boot-wait MUST record a timeout hint and continue to the send attempt; it MUST NOT abort, classify delivery, or return the retired abort path.

acceptance: PASS only if the complete frozen dispatch-canary inventory is enumerated and passes with no skip; removing, renaming away, or not executing any canary fails. Otherwise FAIL.
requirement: Every private Praxis transport change MUST continue to pass the frozen pre-existing dispatch canary suite in addition to tests for the changed behavior.

acceptance: PASS only if syntax-aware/static inspection of every injector path finds zero executable `exit 4` statements and a planted fixture is detected. Otherwise FAIL.
requirement: The private Praxis injector implementation MUST contain no executable `exit 4` path.

acceptance: PASS only if concurrent same-panel sends produce two non-interleaved complete messages under one lock key, different-panel sends can overlap, and stale-lock recovery uses the existing mutex implementation. Otherwise FAIL.
requirement: Private Praxis sends targeting the same panel MUST serialize the entire keystroke-producing critical section through the existing portable per-panel `mt_lock`/`mt_unlock` mutex; sends to different panels MUST remain independent.

acceptance: PASS only if the golden compares every role's embedded and mirrored law, accepts the canonical pair, and fails a one-byte change to either side or a one-sided revision. Otherwise FAIL.
requirement: The private Praxis compiled acknowledgement law and every governed Markdown role-law mirror MUST be byte-equivalent after the declared rendering normalization and MUST change atomically in one revision.

acceptance: PASS only if changed state is green, reverted state is red for the claimed reason, and restored state is green; a check green in both states or red for another reason fails. Otherwise FAIL.
requirement: Private Praxis coverage evidence MUST include a mechanical revert-red control: reverting the claimed causal change while holding the check inputs fixed MUST make the same check fail.

acceptance: PASS only if a fixture with zero exit but absent/wrong effect fails, a fixture whose only diagnostic is stderr preserves and evaluates it, and the correct effect passes. Otherwise FAIL.
requirement: Every private Praxis executor or verifier check MUST preserve stderr and assert the intended observable effect; exit status zero alone MUST NOT satisfy the check.

acceptance: PASS only if evidence orders an applicable RED observation before implementation and GREEN after it; missing RED, postdated RED, or initially green test fails. Otherwise FAIL.
requirement: Private Praxis implementation MUST begin from a failing test or specification check observed before the implementation change; test and implementation MUST NOT be introduced as an already-green pair.

acceptance: PASS only if an actionable fixture records at least one authorized task effect or evidence artifact before the report; narration-only completion fails. Otherwise FAIL.
requirement: A private Praxis executor with an authorized actionable task MUST perform an in-scope state-changing or evidence-producing action rather than ending with narration alone.
